sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashwani Kumar Yadav,Naveen Kumar,Suraj Kumar Singh,Surendra Yad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajesh Kumar Singh,Rakesh Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard Sri Ashwani Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.
No one appeared for the informant.

2. The present second bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 97 of 2020,
under Sections 376 (3) IPC and Section 5g/6 POCSO Act, police station Cholapur, District Varanasi with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The first bail application of applicant was rejected by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 05.01.2021.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
As per ossification test report, the age of victim is 16-1/2 years to 17- 1/2 years.
The allegation that applicant has committed rape upon the victim is wholly false and the same is not supported by the medical evidence.
In medical examination report, no injury has been shown on the body of the victim.
It was stated that applicant has been falsely implicated on account of property dispute.

During trial, only the statement of victim has been Bharosh Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181938304/

sentences.text: recorded before the trial court so far.
Applicant is in jail since 21.03.2020 and thus, he has undergone the detention of about four years.
It was stated that there are number of formal witnesses, who are yet to be examined, and thus trial of the case would take sufficient long time.

Lastly, it was submitted that applicant has no criminal antecedents and that in case applicant is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
4.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that victim is minor girl and she has made allegation of rape against the applicant.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the present second bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Bharosh Kumar involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i.
The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
7. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 15.3.2024/AKT  Bharosh Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181938304/
